title: Unified catalog walkthrough — candidate picks & bench plan (Skyline Health)
summary: Redwood AE + SE ran a catalog and bench planning walkthrough for Skyline Health. Focus was picking 2-3 open models to bench against Skyline's prompt set, interpreting compatibility matrices (kernel/quantization fit), and mapping deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC). Security and compliance (SOC2, KMS, data residency) were raised; next steps center on sharing bench templates, running an initial latency/cost estimate, and scheduling pilot benchmarks.

Skyline to provide representative prompt set and traffic profile

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-08 16:00 UTC | Duration 54m | Recording ID m-20260508-9f3c
Attendees: Eleanor Park (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Singh (Skyline HL), Tom Halpern (CTO), Aisha Brown (Platform)

Summary (auto): quick pass through model catalog UI -> pick 2-3 open models -> plan bench sprint + discuss deployment constraints.

[00:00] Eleanor (Redwood): hey everyone welcome, thanks for making the time. i'm eleanor, i'm the AE on this deal. mateo from our SE team will run the catalog and bench plan with you.
[00:18] Mateo (Redwood SE): hi all, morning/afternoon depending where you are. quick agenda: catalog tour, candidate shortlist logic, bench plan, then q&a on deployment/security.
[00:30] Priya (Skyline): thanks, yea we mainly want to reduce hallucinations on clinical summarization while keeping 100ms-ish p50 token latency where possible, cost matters but accuracy first for the triage flows.
[00:45] Tom (Skyline): and a quick note — we have to keep PHI out of logs, plus we need kms integration and on-prem option for a few sensitive pipelines.
[01:05] Eleanor: great, we'll flag the private deployment path and KMS stuff during the security section. mateo, can you pull up the catalog?
[01:20] Mateo: yep, opening the catalog in console — ok you should see our curated open-model list, i've prefiltered for medically-capable families and quantization-friendly checkpoints. note the compatibility column here — this is where we map kernel/quantization fit to hardware.
[01:40] Mateo: so for skyline i've highlighted two candidates — small-medium size LLM A (open-med-7b) and medium LLM B (general-13b q4f) — both have prior med-domain evals. the matrix shows recommended kernel (cutlass vs triton, approximate) and whether 8-bit quantization degrades rouge/acc in our short bench.
[02:10] Priya: can you explain that compatibility score? sometimes the matrix shows 'partial' or 'mixed' and i'm not sure what that means operationally.
[02:25] Mateo: yeah so we synthesize signals: model architecture tags, our kernel test results, and quantization sensitivity. 'full' means we have optimized kernels and quant paths for that model+hw combo; 'partial' means model runs but may hit slower kernels or require fallback to fp16 for some ops — so expect slightly higher latency or memory footprint. 'mixed' often means the model is asymmetrical — some layers quantize well, others don't, so we recommend a measured bench.
[03:00] Tom: so 'partial' could still be OK if latency targets are met?
[03:08] Eleanor: exactly. that's why benching with your real prompts is the key. our Optimize recommendations will tell you suggested batch sizes and KV cache hints after the initial run.
[03:25] Aisha: question — how does the console suggest batching for low-latency flows? sometimes batching increases p50 substantially.
[03:35] Mateo: the console's Optimize tab gives workload-aware batch suggestions: it looks at your average seq len, QPS, and target p50/p90 to recommend batch config. it also suggests enabling per-route prefix caching for repeated system prompts. but it's always a tradeoff — we show the expected unit-cost impact next to latency.
[04:02] Priya: we're also curious about model quality comparisons — do you have bench suites already for med summarization or do we need to supply those prompts?
[04:15] Mateo: we have public reference suites and med-oriented evaluation sets but for clinical sensitivity you'll want to run your own labeled prompts. for the sprint we'll take your prompt set + our baseline and run accuracy + safety checks.
[04:30] Eleanor: note that for the pilot we usually pick 2 candidates: one lower-cost quantized variant and one higher-capacity baseline, that helps with the latency/cost/quality tradeoff.
[04:48] Priya: ok, makes sense. can the console track eval regressions over time? we want alerts if new rollouts worsen F1.
[04:58] Mateo: yes, our Console Eval hooks will compute your metrics per-deploy and send regression alerts. we can wire your slack/email and tie to rollouts — if a canary drops below threshold we'll auto-fallback to previous variant.
[05:20] Tom: about deployment: our security team will want a private deployment option, and we might start with dedicated capacity then move to on-prem. is that supported?
[05:33] Eleanor: absolutely — hosted for quick experiments then dedicated reserved pools for production, or private with VPC/on-prem for the regulated pipelines. we'll share the matrix of feature parity across those modes.
[05:48] Aisha: does your private offering allow customer KMS and audit logs? we need HSM-backed keys ideally.
[05:56] Mateo: yes, private supports customer-managed KMS keys and full audit logs; for on-prem we can support HSM integration as part of the enterprise package. we'll include the compliance checklist in the security docs we send.
[06:15] Priya: any limitations on embeddings or reranking when we use quantized models?
[06:24] Mateo: embeddings are generally FP16-safe but heavy quantization can slightly change vector distances — we recommend separate benching for embedding recall. for reranking, we often use a two-stage approach: cheap embedding+approximate ranker then rerank with the higher-fidelity model.
[06:40] Eleanor: back to the catalog, i'm going to show the compatibility heatmap — it aggregates kernel match, memory fit, and prior bench signal. you'll see the two candidates highlighted with expected token/s on our typical A100 and M1200 profiles.
[07:05] Mateo: there's also a notes column where our Model Ops team has added caveats like 'attention pattern causes kv-cache blow up past 2k tokens' — that matters for your long discharge summaries.
[07:28] Aisha: oh that note is helpful — some of our summaries are 3k tokens. what would you recommend?
[07:36] Mateo: if you hit >2k regularly, we recommend either model variants with optimized KV cache or segmentation in the pipeline + streaming. another option is to keep long-context models for indexing and use short-context models for on-the-fly summarization.
[07:55] Priya: can you do a quick bench plan outline now? we have about 2 weeks of runway for an initial sprint.
[08:05] Mateo: yes — suggested plan: week 0 (this week) collect prompt set + traffic profile, week 1 run parallel bench: ingest prompts into our bench harness across 2 candidates on your chosen hw profile, collect p50/p90, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy metrics; week 2 analyze and pick pilot candidate + plan rollout. we'll provide the harness and scripts; you'll run in hosted or dedicated depending on comfort, or we can run in our infra with obfuscated prompts if you prefer.
[08:38] Eleanor: practical note — for initial speed we often run synthetic sampling to pre-filter obviously bad candidates then run full labeled eval on the top 3. this halves time.
[08:50] Tom: what about data residency for logs from bench runs?
[08:55] Mateo: bench runs can be configured to not persist prompts, or we can run within your VPC so data never leaves your network. we'll set that up per your preference.
[09:10] Aisha: i like the idea of obfuscated runs first. how do we integrate with your bench harness? is there a repo?
[09:18] Mateo: yes, we have a bench repo + a console upload flow; i'll share a drive link with instructions. it's basically a csv of prompts with expected outputs/metrics and a small runner.
[09:28] Priya: on the compatibility matrix again — sometimes the matrix rank and the actual bench results disagree, is that common?
[09:35] Mateo: it happens because the matrix is a heuristic combining many signals. that's why the process is heuristic -> bench -> interpret. the console also stores run artifacts and maps matrix deltas to real-run deltas so over time our matrix improves.
[09:58] Eleanor: quick interruption — question from legal/security: what SOC2 scope do you cover and can you share the attestation?
[10:06] Mateo: we have SOC2 Type II for the hosted control plane; Dedicated adds contractual SLAs and Private has a separate compliance package — we'll attach the attestation and the private deployment compliance checklist.
[10:20] Tom: ok, please include the SOC2 report and a high-level network architecture for VPC/private.
[10:28] Eleanor: noted, we'll send both.
[10:33] Priya: one more on model updates — how do rollouts handle model-version regressions? we can't have a sudden drop during peak hours.
[10:41] Mateo: we recommend canary rollouts with metric gates done through the console; if the canary fails, automatic fallback triggers. you can configure thresholds per metric (accuracy, latency, error-rate).
[10:56] Aisha: will the console show side-by-side bench comparisons?
[11:02] Mateo: yes, we'll produce a bench report with side-by-side plots for latency, cost, and accuracy. it also flags potential quantization artifacts.
[11:18] Eleanor: switching to a brief live demo — i'm going to create a shortlist filter: here i'm filtering on 'medical', 'compatibility: full or partial', 'quantization: q4f supported'. you can see candidate tags, kernel recommendation, and bench history.
[11:40] Priya: I see a 'fallback variants' section — what does that look like in production?
[11:46] Mateo: fallback variants are lighter or older models you can use when the primary variant is unavailable or exceeds latency SLOs. routing policies in Smart Routing can prefer lower-cost variants for non-critical traffic.
[12:02] Tom: curious about pricing — if we run a bench in hosted mode for the pilot is there a cost surcharge?
[12:10] Eleanor: bench runs in hosted mode are billed at normal usage rates; for larger bench sprints we can offer credits or pilot terms — we'll include pricing options.
[12:22] Priya: can we request local hardware mapping? for example we target an M1200 profile in prod. will your kernel mapping match?
[12:30] Mateo: yes, our kernel map includes common GPUs and we can add custom target profiles; that helps the compatibility matrix be more precise for your infra.
[12:42] Aisha: back to the bench harness — for accuracy metrics do you support BLEU/F1/custom scripts?
[12:49] Mateo: we support custom metrics, and you can plug in your scorer or use our built-in metrics. we store metric code as part of the bench artifact so it's reproducible.
[13:00] Priya: great. any gotchas you want to call out for med summarization specifically?
[13:07] Mateo: watch out for dataset leakage where the model was pre-trained on similar clinical data; we can run membership tests. also quantization can sometimes increase tokenization oddities around uncommon medical abbreviations, so check token-level diffs.
[13:28] Tom: can we see an example bench report?
[13:32] Mateo: opening a sample in the console — here's a comparison of candidate A (q4f) vs candidate B (fp16 base). notice tradeoffs: A lowers cost ~40% but drops F1 by 3 points on our summarization set; p90 latency improves slightly with A on GPU profile X.
[13:55] Priya: that delta is acceptable depending on error modes — can you show confusion examples?
[14:02] Mateo: yes we have an examples tab — it surfaces cases where outputs differ and highlights hallucinations. we'll include that in the report.
[14:15] Eleanor: more on project mechanics: we'll do an initial sync to confirm prompts and QPS, then a 2-week bench sprint, then a wrap with recommended pilot variant and rollout plan.
[14:30] Aisha: timeframe sounds doable. who's the primary point for bench ops?
[14:35] Eleanor: mateo will lead bench ops on our side; aisha/priya from skyline will coordinate data & scoring.
[14:44] Priya: ok. one more security nuance — we need proof that bench artifacts can be purged on demand. is that possible?
[14:52] Mateo: yes, artifacts can be configured with TTL and manual purge; for private we can ensure they never leave your VPC.
[15:05] Tom: i'm going to ask about autoscaling — if we go dedicated, how do we handle burst traffic?
[15:14] Mateo: dedicated pools support configured autoscaling and burst capacity; you set min and burst headroom. if burst exceeds pool capacity, Smart Routing can failover to hosted variants if policy allows.
[15:30] Priya: can we configure cost controls? want to avoid runaway spend during peaks.
[15:36] Eleanor: yes, we have token-level budgets, per-route quotas and alerting, and you can set hard caps.
[15:47] Aisha: small question — are function calls or tooling supported in quantized models?
[15:55] Mateo: basic function calling is supported but heavy tool-chaining may require fp16 runs; we'll mark those in the compatibility notes.
[16:05] Eleanor: going to capture next steps — we'll share bench template, security docs, and a sample bench report. mateo will run an initial latency-cost estimate.
[16:18] Priya: thanks, also please include sample network diagrams for dedicated and private deployments.
[16:24] Eleanor: noted.
[16:28] Tom: okay let's wrap — appreciate the demo, excited to start the bench sprint.
[16:32] Eleanor: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the kickoff.

[End of recording — total ~54 minutes]
